newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude markets quiet as outright swings.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude markets quiet as outright swings.

text.p: As outright prices for October Brent swung in an 85 cent range on Tuesday, traders stepped back and little action was seen either on the paper or wet markets.
"It's all a bit too much like a casino putting your money in oil at the moment. We're waiting until it all calms down again," a trader with a major oil company said.
As futures traders took profits following the early rally, outright October Brent crude fell back to just above the day's lows to trade at 1532 GMT up six cents on the day at $22.05 a barrel.
Intermonth spreads followed with talk on Sep/Oct Brent around +65 cents and November/December down to +70/75 cents.
All three Brent cargoes in Tuesday's chains were still being passed, traders said.
Sellers of wet crude were offering at October +25 cents but bids were coming in ten cents lower. The market was assessed around +20 cents following Monday's deals at +15 cents.

Remaining middle decade September cargoes were under some pressure with at least three Statfjord and three Oseberg cargoes still for sale in this period. Offers were coming from dated Brent +25-30 cents. Potential buyers were holding back.
"Sellers' ideas went too high with the earlier rally and have not come down enough yet," one commented.
Ekofisk held firm with only end month cargoes remaining and the market was assessed around dated Brent +40 cents.
Talk on CFD's was very limited with little interest in the remainder of this week and next weeks Sept 9-13 dates discussed at October +12/+15 cents.
